findings.note: Doc comment contradicts actual canonical form: canonical.go says HTML characters and U+2028/U+2029 are "left as literal UTF-8", but marshalCanonical only disables HTML escaping — Go's encoder still escapes the line separators. Empirically Canonical("{\"a\":\"\u2028<\"}") returns {"a":"\u2028<"}, and canonical_test.go:22 asserts exactly that escaped form. The implementation and its tests agree; only the docstring (and the same sentence in docs/specs/2026-08-26-metareview-0.9.0-fsm-run-persistence.md:122) is wrong. Non-blocking, but it would mislead any reimplementation of the hash contract, and encodedRuneLen's 6-byte case already encodes the true behavior.

evidence.note: "with HTML characters and U+2028/U+2029 left as literal UTF-8" — U+2028/U+2029 are in fact escaped to \u2028/\u2029 by the shared marshalCanonical encoder
encodedRuneLen counts U+2028/U+2029 as 6 bytes, i.e. escaped — directly contradicting the file's own Canonical doc comment
